knowledge_point.title: Computing an Integral Using the Sum Rule

question.:question/worked-solution:
Applying the sum rule, we compute the sum of the integrals of each function:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \left(-6-x^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x &= \int \left(-6-x^{2}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &= -6\int 1\,\mathrm{d}x-\int x^{2}\,\mathrm{d}x \\ &= -6\frac{x^{0+1}}{(0+1)}-\frac{x^{2+1}}{(2+1)}+C \\ &= -6x-\frac{x^{3}}{3}+C\end{aligned}
$$
